digest.top_line: STELLAR: 5x5 Gy + CAPOX TNT non-inferior on 3-yr DFS (64.5% v 62.3%, HR 0.883) with 3-yr OS 86.5% v 75.1% (HR 0.67).
digest.tldr: Two Chinese phase 3 TNT trials land the same week and split on where the gain comes from: STELLAR's 5x5 short-course buys OS (86.5% v 75.1%) with no LRR or DM signal behind it, while TNTCRT's long-course doublet buys distant control (MFS HR 0.655) with locoregional failure flat at ~6% in both arms. Lower GI carried the day; prostate was PSMA PET imaging, not therapy.

sites.intro: Both TNT trials leave locoregional control untouched vs nCRT, so the RT question is now sequencing and fractionation, not whether pelvic RT is doing the work.

studies.name: STELLAR
studies.tldr: 3-yr DFS 64.5% vs 62.3% (HR 0.883, NI margin 1.43) for 5x5 Gy + CAPOX vs 50 Gy/25f CRT in LARC.
details: 🔍 Multicenter open-label phase III, 16 Chinese hospitals, N=599 randomized 1:1, ITT; median f/u 35.0 mo
🔍 cT3-4 and/or cN+ distal/middle-third rectal adenocarcinoma, age 18-70, ECOG 0-1, MRI-staged centrally by 3 radiologists
📐 NI margin prespecified at HR 1.43 (equivalently 3-yr DFS ≥54% assuming 65% in CRT arm), one-sided alpha 0.05, ≥194 DFS events

details.text: 📊 3-yr efficacy, TNT (5 Gy x5 → 4 CAPOX) vs CRT (50 Gy/25f + capecitabine)

rows: HR 0.883, one-sided 95% CI to 1.11, P<.001 NI

details: 📐 All TNT pts completed 5 Gy x5 without dose reduction; CRT arm had 1.4% RT dose reduction, 2.4% interruption

🔍 IMRT in ALL pts, both arms: CTV mesorectum, presacral, internal iliac, obturator, ischiorectal fossa; external iliac only if cT4b; superior border sacral promontory, inferior 2-3 cm below tumor; PTV expansion 0.5-1.0 cm

details.text: ⚠️ Acute grade 3-4 toxicity during preop treatment, 26.5% vs 12.6% (P<.001), driven by heme not bowel

details: 📊 Preop full-dose completion 74.8% TNT vs 93.2% CRT (P<.001); adjuvant chemo completion 60.0% vs 48.3% (P=.009)
🔗 3-yr LRR 8.4%/11.0% in line with RAPIDO and PRODIGE 23 (4%-8.3%), far below Polish II (21%-22%), the only one of the four without mandated adjuvant chemo
⚠️ OS gain is a secondary endpoint on 107 cancer deaths, not powered for it; authors note Polish II's OS benefit vanished by 8 yr
⚠️ Unlike RAPIDO and PRODIGE 23, no 3-yr DM reduction with TNT (22.8% v 24.7%), so the OS signal has no MFS or LRR mechanism behind it
⚠️ Chinese-only cohort, age capped at 70 (median 55), middle/low rectum only; upper rectum untested

verdict.rationale: Prespecified noninferiority met in a randomized phase III with adequate events. Consistent with Polish II and RAPIDO; supports an already guideline-listed short-course TNT option.
verdict.audience: cT3-4 and/or cN+ distal/middle-third rectal adenocarcinoma, age ≤70, ECOG 0-1

studies.significance: Every pt got IMRT, both arms, and 3-yr LRR was 8.4% with 5 Gy x5 alone, so the elective-nodal CTV (mesorectum, presacral, internal iliac, obturator, ischiorectal fossa) holds at a hypofractionated dose. The added grade 3-4 toxicity was hematologic (15.8% v 2.0%), from the CAPOX, not the pelvis: proctitis and diarrhea were flat.
studies.monday_clinic: In cT3-4 or node-positive middle or distal rectal cancer under age 70 with good performance status, this supports 5 Gy x5 plus preop CAPOX as an alternative to 50 Gy/25f chemoradiation; it does not address upper-third tumors, and late toxicity and organ-preservation durability are not yet reported.

primary_endpoint.name: 3-year disease-free survival
primary_endpoint.stat_detail: HR 0.883, one-sided 95% CI to 1.11, P<.001 for noninferiority (margin 1.43)

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Multicenter open-label randomized phase III, 1:1, **N=599** across 16 hospitals in 11 Chinese provinces, enrolled Aug 2015 to Aug 2018. Stratified by location, clinical stage, and MRF status; median follow-up **35.0 months** (range 8.3-63.9).

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: **cT3-4 and/or cN+** rectal adenocarcinoma of the distal or middle third, age **18-70**, ECOG 0-1, no distant metastases, no prior anticancer treatment. Median age 55, **85.8% v 83.5% clinical stage III**, MRF involvement in ~56% of both arms; EMVI was imbalanced (53.4% TNT v 42.1% CRT).

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: TNT arm: **5 Gy x 5** over one week. CRT arm: **50 Gy in 25 fractions** over 5 weeks with concurrent capecitabine 825 mg/m² BID. **All patients received IMRT** in both arms, with CTV covering mesorectum, presacral space, internal iliac, obturator, and ischiorectal fossa (external iliac only for cT4b), superior border at the sacral promontory, inferior 2-3 cm distal to the tumor, PTV expansion 0.5-1.0 cm, with per-center QA.

analysis_sections.label: Regimen
analysis_sections.body: TNT: **4 cycles CAPOX** (oxaliplatin 130 mg/m² d1, capecitabine 1,000 mg/m² BID d1-14) starting 7-14 days after RT, then TME, then 2 further CAPOX cycles. CRT: concurrent capecitabine, then TME, then **6 cycles CAPOX**. TME was recommended 6-8 weeks after preoperative treatment in both arms.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: **Primary: 3-year DFS**, noninferiority with a prespecified **HR margin of 1.43** (an 11% absolute margin against an assumed 65% CRT rate), one-sided alpha 0.05, powered at ≥194 events. Secondary: OS, MFS, locoregional recurrence, surgical complications, toxicity, completion rate, and pCR plus sustained cCR.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: Noninferiority was met, and the OS difference favoring TNT is a secondary finding resting on 107 cancer deaths with no accompanying MFS or LRR separation. Sustained cCR without surgery reached **9.4% v 3.4%**, with regrowth in 2 of 28 and 1 of 10 respectively.

analysis_sections.label: Safety
analysis_sections.body: Acute grade III-V toxicity during preoperative treatment was **26.5% v 12.6%** (P<.001), almost entirely hematologic (grade 3-4 heme **15.8% v 2.0%**, thrombocytopenia 11.1% v 0.7%). Pelvic toxicity did not differ (proctitis G3-4 4.7% v 3.1%, diarrhea 6.4% v 4.8%), and grade III+ surgical complications were similar (14.0% v 15.7%, P=.625).

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: The third randomized trial of short-course RT plus chemotherapy against long-course CRT. **LRR 8.4%/11.0%** matches RAPIDO and PRODIGE 23 (4%-8.3%) and is well below Polish II (21%-22%), but unlike RAPIDO and PRODIGE 23 there was **no 3-year DM reduction** (22.8% v 24.7%). The OS gain echoes Polish II, where the benefit disappeared by 8 years.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents cT3-4 or node-positive middle and distal rectal cancer in patients aged 70 or younger with ECOG 0-1 treated with IMRT. Does not represent upper-third rectal tumors, patients over 70, or those needing a non-oxaliplatin systemic backbone.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: Late toxicity and quality of life are deferred to a later report, so the durable pelvic cost of 5 Gy x 5 with IMRT is still unmeasured. The one-sided noninferiority CI with an upper bound of 1.11 against a 1.43 margin leaves room for a real DFS decrement, and the authors concede a narrower margin or larger sample would have been preferable. EMVI was imbalanced toward the TNT arm at baseline (53.4% v 42.1%).

significance_by_specialty.radonc: 5 Gy x 5 delivered by IMRT to a full elective pelvic CTV gave 3-yr LRR of 8.4%, so nodal coverage holds at the hypofractionated dose and every patient completed RT without reduction. The excess grade 3-4 toxicity was hematologic (15.8% v 2.0%) from CAPOX, with proctitis and diarrhea flat, so the pelvis is not what you are trading away, at least on acute data.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: Moving chemotherapy preoperatively raised planned-cycle completion (74.8% full-dose preop, and 60.0% v 48.3% completing adjuvant), but 4 cycles of CAPOX bought no distant metastasis reduction (22.8% v 24.7%), unlike the more intensive FOLFOX or FOLFIRINOX backbones in RAPIDO and PRODIGE 23. The toxicity cost was hematologic and front-loaded.
significance_by_specialty.surgonc: R0 resection was 91.5% v 87.8% (P=.189) and grade III+ surgical complications 14.0% v 15.7% (P=.625), so short-course RT with a 21-week median interval from RT start to surgery did not compromise the operation. Sustained cCR managed nonoperatively was 9.4% v 3.4%, relevant to organ-preservation discussions, though regrowth data are thin (2 of 28).

open_questions: Durability of the OS difference beyond 3 years
Late toxicity and quality of life after 5 Gy x 5 plus CAPOX
Whether more preoperative chemotherapy cycles reduce distant metastasis

studies.name: TNTCRT
studies.tldr: 3-yr DFS 74.8% v 66.0%, HR 0.674, for doublet-CAPOX TNT vs nCRT in high-risk LARC; locoregional failure unchanged.

details.text: 📊 Efficacy by arm (3-yr rates unless noted)
📊 Toxicity and surgical morbidity by arm

details: 🔍 Phase 3, N=458 (232 v 226), accrued 2017-2023, median f/u 51 mo, age 18-70

subdetails: TNT: induction CAPOX x1 → LCRT + concurrent CAPOX x2 → consolidation CAPOX x3 → TME
nCRT: LCRT + concurrent capecitabine → TME → adjuvant CAPOX x6 at 4-8 wks

details: 📐 LCRT in both arms; RT dose, fractionation, target volume not reported in source text
⚠️ DFS gain rests on distant control; OS curves have not separated at 3 years
⚠️ Age capped at 70; author states benefit-risk above that needs further study
🔗 Source names RAPIDO, PRODIGE-23, STELLAR as TNT precedents; no head-to-head data

verdict.rationale: Randomized phase 3, primary DFS met at 51-mo median f/u, but TNT is already established by RAPIDO/PRODIGE-23/STELLAR; adds a regimen option, not a paradigm.
verdict.audience: High-risk stage II/III LARC (cT4, cN2, MRF+, or EMVI+), age ≤70

studies.significance: Locoregional failure was identical (6.03% v 6.19%, P=.943) with the entire chemo course moved preoperatively, so intensifying systemic therapy around LCRT costs nothing in local control. RT dose, fractionation and target volume are absent from the source text, which gates transfer. The decision this moves is chemo sequencing, not RT technique.
studies.monday_clinic: In high-risk stage II/III rectal cancer aged 70 or under with cT4, cN2, involved mesorectal fascia, or EMVI, this supports delivering the full CAPOX course before surgery rather than adjuvantly; it does not extend to pts over 70 or to stage II/III disease without a high-risk MRI feature.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Multicenter **randomized phase 3**, N=458, accrual June 2017 to December 2023, median follow-up **51 months**. Blinding is not stated in the source.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: Stage II/III LARC aged **18 to 70** with at least 1 MRI high-risk feature (cT4a-b, cN2, involved mesorectal fascia, or cT3c-d with EMVI). Baseline burden was heavy on every axis, with **cN2 in 75.98%** and a **threatened MRF in 70.96%**.

analysis_sections.label: Regimen
analysis_sections.body: Doublet-LC TNT: **1 cycle induction CAPOX**, LCRT with **2 cycles concurrent CAPOX**, **3 cycles consolidation CAPOX**, then surgery. Control: LCRT with **concurrent capecitabine**, surgery, then **6 cycles adjuvant CAPOX** starting 4 to 8 weeks postoperatively.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: **LCRT in both arms**, so radiotherapy is held constant and the randomization tests chemotherapy intensity and sequencing around it. **Dose, fractionation and target volume are not reported in the source text.** Roughly **87%** of TNT pts and **90%** of nCRT pts went on to total mesorectal excision.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: **Primary: disease-free survival.** Secondary endpoints included MFS, pCR, locoregional failure, overall survival, and toxicity across the neoadjuvant phase and the whole treatment course.

analysis_sections.label: Safety
analysis_sections.body: The excess grade ≥3 toxicity is confined to the **neoadjuvant phase**; across the full treatment course, and for major postoperative complications, the arms converge, because the control arm pays its chemotherapy cost after surgery instead.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: The source names **RAPIDO, PRODIGE-23 and STELLAR** as the phase 3 TNT precedents but reports no cross-trial numbers. The phase 2 precursor of this regimen reported a complete response rate of **36.2%**.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents high-risk stage II/III LARC aged 18 to 70 with cT4, cN2, involved mesorectal fascia, or EMVI. Does not represent pts over 70, or stage II/III disease carrying no high-risk MRI feature.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: The DFS interval reaches **0.929** and OS shows no separation, so the benefit rests on distant control with a modest margin. Late toxicity, function and quality of life are still pending per the authors, which matters for a regimen whose whole cost is delivered upfront.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: Locoregional failure was identical (6.03% v 6.19%), so moving the whole CAPOX course preoperatively costs nothing in local control while pCR rises to 26.37%, enlarging the pool for a watch-and-wait discussion. RT dose, fractionation and target volume are absent from the source text, which gates transfer.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: The variable here is chemotherapy, not radiotherapy: uninterrupted doublet CAPOX delivered entirely before surgery beat capecitabine chemoRT plus 6 adjuvant CAPOX cycles on DFS and MFS. The excess grade ≥3 toxicity sits in the neoadjuvant phase only and converges across the full course.
significance_by_specialty.surgonc: Intensified preoperative therapy did not degrade the operation: major postoperative complications were 3.98% v 2.94%, and roughly 87% versus 90% of pts proceeded to total mesorectal excision. The pCR jump to 26.37% is the number that will drive organ-preservation conversations at MDT.

open_questions: Doublet-LC TNT versus short-course RT-based TNT regimens head to head
Benefit-risk of intensified TNT in pts over 70
Whether the higher pCR translates into durable organ preservation

sites.intro: Both entries are PSMA PET interpretation, not treatment: what a positive scan in BCR obligates, and whether uptake change can be read as response at all.

studies.name: PSMA PET BCR Natural History Study
studies.tldr: Baseline data on 130 PSMA-positive BCR men; most with PSADT >9-12mo still had PET findings, yet only ~1/3 started therapy.
details: 🔍 Prospective NCI natural-history cohort, N=130 at baseline; ongoing, median f/u ~2yr
🔍 Eligibility: post-definitive therapy BCR, PSA ≥0.5, salvage RT already given or declined
🔍 Imaging schedule: baseline PSMA PET; negative → annual, any finding (incl equivocal) → q6mo
📊 Majority with PSADT >9mo and >12mo had PSMA PET findings when PSA was above 5
📊 Sites of disease described as nodal, prostate bed recurrence, occasional small equivocal bone lesions
📊 Only about a third have gone on therapy so far; majority observed off treatment

details.text: 📊 Progression on conventional imaging (companion Madan poster, ~1.5yr f/u)
subdetails: 5 patients out of the first ~150 progressed on conventional imaging
Stated >95% had no abrupt PET change discordant from PSA kinetics

details: 🔍 Therapy on study limited to courses <6mo: intermittent ADT, intermittent ARPI trials, Radium-223, SBRT allowed
⚠️ Designed pre-EMBARK, so the observation arm predates current BCR treatment norms
⚠️ Source is a conference interview transcript, not a peer-reviewed report; no CIs, no denominators for the PSADT strata
⚠️ Selection bias: NCI referral cohort, patients willing to be observed; not a consecutive registry

verdict.rationale: Baseline cross-sectional read of an ongoing single-institution cohort; no comparator, no outcome endpoint yet, numbers reported only as narrative in an interview.
verdict.audience: PSMA-positive biochemical recurrence, post-salvage RT or RT declined, PSA ≥0.5

studies.significance: The RT-relevant read is that a positive PET at PSA >5 is near-universal even at PSADT >12mo, so PET positivity alone does not identify who needs metastasis-directed SBRT. Prostate bed recurrence was among the described sites, which reopens a salvage-RT target question in men already treated with salvage RT.
studies.monday_clinic: In post-salvage-RT BCR men with slow PSADT and a positive PSMA PET, this supports observation as a defensible option pending follow-up data; it does not speak to men with rapid PSADT or conventional-imaging metastases.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Prospective **natural history** cohort at the NCI, ongoing, median follow-up **~2 years**. The reported analysis is **baseline imaging of the first 130 patients**, a single timepoint correlating PSMA PET findings with PSA doubling time.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: Men with **BCR after definitive therapy**, all of whom had already received **salvage radiation or declined it**. Entry requires **PSA ≥0.5**; these are patients who would not have qualified for metastatic trials before PSMA PET existed.

analysis_sections.label: Regimen
analysis_sections.body: Therapy is **physician's choice, not mandated**, and capped at courses lasting **under six months**: intermittent ADT, intermittent ARPI protocols, a Radium-223 trial, or SBRT. **Only about a third** have started any therapy.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: SBRT is permitted as a **short-course option**, not protocol-mandated; no dose, fractionation, or target-volume detail is reported in source. All enrollees are **post-salvage RT or salvage-RT decliners**, so the prostate bed has usually already been treated.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: The presented analysis is descriptive: **PSMA PET positivity versus PSA doubling time** at baseline. Longitudinal endpoints (PET evolution, conventional-imaging progression) are stated as still being analyzed.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: The **majority** of men with PSADT **>9mo and >12mo** had PSMA PET findings once **PSA exceeded 5**, chiefly nodal, prostate bed, and small equivocal bone lesions. In the companion follow-up poster, **5 of the first ~150** progressed on conventional imaging at about 1.5 years.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents PSMA-positive BCR after definitive therapy plus salvage RT, PSA ≥0.5, largely favorable PSA kinetics. Does not represent conventionally metastatic disease, de novo mCSPC, or men who have never had salvage RT considered.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: Numbers reach the reader only through an interview transcript: no stratum denominators, no confidence intervals, no per-PSADT-band positivity rates. The **five progression events** come from a separate poster on an overlapping but differently sized cohort (~150), so it cannot be aligned to the 130-patient baseline set.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: The stated framing is that PSMA-positive BCR is a **new disease state**, visible only because the scan changed, and that treating it as mCSPC risks **overtreatment** in men who historically waited years for conventional metastases. The cohort's value will be longitudinal, whether PET change adds anything over PSA kinetics.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: Near-universal PET positivity at PSA >5, even at PSADT >12mo, means a positive scan by itself cannot select men for metastasis-directed SBRT. Prostate bed recurrence appears among described sites in a cohort already given salvage RT, which bears on re-irradiation and target questions.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: Only about a third started therapy and 5 of ~150 progressed on conventional imaging at ~1.5yr, arguing against reflexively applying mCSPC doublet or triplet approaches to PSMA-detected BCR. It supports observation or intermittent short-course therapy while awaiting longitudinal data.

studies.significance: Serial PSMA PET after starting abiraterone or enzalutamide reads AR signaling, not burden, so a post-treatment scan is not a response map. The stratification is real (median OS 17.8 vs 37.2 mo by DPSM) but prognostic, and RECIP 1.0 was built for radioligand therapy, not AR-axis agents.
studies.monday_clinic: In men with metastatic APMR restaged on PSMA PET 2 to 4 months after starting abiraterone or enzalutamide, an increase in uptake is prognostic but not established as progression; it does not extend to men whose PSMA PET follows radioligand therapy.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: PSMA PET drives metastasis-directed target selection, and this argues the post-AR-agent scan is not a burden map: uptake moves with androgen receptor signaling. RECIP 1.0 was designed for radioligand therapy response, so the source does not extend it to scans taken after abiraterone or enzalutamide.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: The switch decision is the point: high DPSM carried median time to therapy change 6.5 mo vs 12.2 mo for low DPSM (p=0.0001), so the pattern stratifies prognosis. It does not establish that increased uptake at 2 to 4 months equals progression warranting a change of AR-axis agent.

papers.title: Total Neoadjuvant Therapy With Long-Course Radiotherapy Versus Chemoradiotherapy in High-Risk Locally Advanced Rectal Cancer (TNTCRT): A Multicenter, Randomized, Phase III Trial
papers.abstract: PURPOSE High-risk locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC) carries a substantial risk of distant recurrence, which limits disease-free survival (DFS). We compared total neoadjuvant therapy (TNT) integrating long-course radiotherapy (LCRT) with uninterrupted doublet chemotherapy (doublet-LC TNT) versus conventional neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (nCRT). METHODS In this multicenter, randomized, phase III trial, patients with stage II/III LARC and at least 1 high-risk feature (cT4a-b, cN2, mesorectal fascia involvement, or cT3c-d with extramural vascular invasion) were enrolled. Patients were assigned to doublet-LC TNT (induction, concurrent, and consolidation capecitabine plus oxaliplatin with LCRT) before surgery or nCRT (capecitabine with LCRT) followed by surgery and adjuvant chemotherapy. The primary end point was DFS (ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT03177382 ). RESULTS Between June 6, 2017, and December 27, 2023, 458 patients were randomly assigned to doublet-LC TNT (n = 232) or nCRT (n = 226). At a median follow-up of 51 months, doublet-LC TNT improved 3-year DFS (74.8% v 66.0%; hazard ratio [HR], 0.674 [95% CI, 0.489 to 0.929]; P = .016). Metastasis-free survival (MFS; 77.7% v 67.6%; HR, 0.655 [95% CI, 0.469 to 0.915]) and pathologic complete response rates (pCR; 26.37% v 9.80%; P < .001) were higher with doublet-LC TNT, whereas locoregional failure remained low and comparable (6.03% v 6.19%; P = .943). Although grade ≥3 adverse events during the neoadjuvant phase were more frequent with doublet-LC TNT (27.59% v 8.56%; P < .001), severe toxicities during the entire treatment course (28.02% v 24.32%; P = .371) and major postoperative complications (3.98% v 2.94%; P = .567) were comparable. CONCLUSION Compared with conventional nCRT, doublet-LC TNT improved DFS, MFS, and pCR rates with manageable toxicity. These findings support this intensified, doublet-based regimen as a standard option within the modern TNT paradigm. Further comparative studies are warranted to evaluate these results against other short-course radiotherapy‑based or nondoublet-concurrent TNT regimens.

papers.title: Multicenter, Randomized, Phase III Trial of Short-Term Radiotherapy Plus Chemotherapy Versus Long-Term Chemoradiotherapy in Locally Advanced Rectal Cancer (STELLAR)
papers.abstract: PURPOSE To ascertain if preoperative short-term radiotherapy followed by chemotherapy is not inferior to a standard schedule of long-term chemoradiotherapy in patients with locally advanced rectal cancer. MATERIALS AND METHODS Patients with distal or middle-third, clinical primary tumor stage 3-4 and/or regional lymph node–positive rectal cancer were randomly assigned (1:1) to short-term radiotherapy (25 Gy in five fractions over 1 week) followed by four cycles of chemotherapy (total neoadjuvant therapy [TNT]) or chemoradiotherapy (50 Gy in 25 fractions over 5 weeks, concurrently with capecitabine [chemoradiotherapy; CRT]). Total mesorectal excision was undertaken 6-8 weeks after preoperative treatment, with two additional cycles of CAPOX (intravenous oxaliplatin [130 mg/m 2 , once a day] on day 1 and capecitabine [1,000 mg/m 2 , twice a day] from days 1 to 14) in the TNT group and six cycles of CAPOX in the CRT group. The primary end point was 3-year disease-free survival (DFS). RESULTS Between August 2015 and August 2018, a total of 599 patients were randomly assigned to receive TNT (n = 302) or CRT (n = 297). At a median follow-up of 35.0 months, 3-year DFS was 64.5% and 62.3% in TNT and CRT groups, respectively (hazard ratio, 0.883; one-sided 95% CI, not applicable to 1.11; P < .001 for noninferiority). There was no significant difference in metastasis-free survival or locoregional recurrence, but the TNT group had better 3-year overall survival than the CRT group (86.5% v 75.1%; P = .033). Treatment effects on DFS and overall survival were similar regardless of prognostic factors. The prevalence of acute grade III-V toxicities during preoperative treatment was 26.5% in the TNT group versus 12.6% in the CRT group ( P < .001). CONCLUSION Short-term radiotherapy with preoperative chemotherapy followed by surgery was efficacious with acceptable toxicity and could be used as an alternative to CRT for locally advanced rectal cancer.
